newsitem.title: USA: Inland Steel contract offer approved.
newsitem.headline: Inland Steel contract offer approved.

text.p: Inland Steel Industries Inc's contract offer for the United Steelworkers of America was approved by an arbitrator, the company said Tuesday.
The contract covers some 7,000 employees at the Indiana Harbor Works in East Chicago and the Minorca Mine in Virginia, Minn. The decision followed a five-day arbitration hearing last month.
The contract covers the second half of a six-year agreement with the steelworkers, which runs through July 31, 1999. The company and the union had agreed to reopen the contract mid-term.
The two did not reach a settlement on their own, so as agreed each submitted a final offer to an arbitrator, who chose Inland Steel's, the company said.
Steelworkers at Inland will receive wage increases of $0.50 an hour retroactive to August 1, and an additional $0.25 a hour on August 1, 1997 and August 1, 1998, the company said.
In addition, lump sums of $1,000 will be paid in each of the three contract years, and workers will receive one additional holiday and increased retirement benefits, Inland said.
